reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology models soccer match outcomes through latent shot-level distributions—quantity and quality—conditioned on ELO ratings. Shot quantity is modeled as a normal distribution with mean and variance functions of ELO differentials. Similarly, shot quality (goals per shot) is modeled as another normal distribution. These distributions are sampled to simulate match outcomes. The approach avoids closed-form scoreline models by leveraging generative simulation pipelines. It assumes independence between quantity and quality, which may not hold in practice. The method uses linear regression in submission but tests other algorithms. Validation includes correctness of score predictions and calibration against market consensus. The framework is adaptable to NFL metrics such as plays per game and EPA per play, where similar distributional assumptions apply. However, the model suffers from mis-specification of shot count distributions (should be negative binomial), lack of dependency modeling, and potential leakage in validation splits. The simulation process introduces bias if underlying assumptions about normality and independence are violated.
